We present a theoretical framework establishing conditions under which attractor dynamics dominate adversarial policies, supported by extensive empirical validation. Our results demonstrate a critical threshold attractor strength (k* ≈ 2.5) beyond which all agents inevitably converge to the attractor regardless of their escape strategies.
